Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity desktop web application screen for "MeteoSurf Cs", edge to edge, landscape 16:10, crisp Spanish typography, no browser frame or physical device. This is a working marine forecasting application for surf schools, coaches and clubs planning a session, NOT marketing and NOT a school management dashboard.
User brief: meticulous contemporary Apple application-like design, restrained light theme, clean system sans, precise aligned numerals, white work surface and pale cool-gray navigation, meaningful blue selection, no glass, no gradient backgrounds, no decorative metric tiles. The distinctive functional feature is one shared selected time window across multiple surf spots.
Screen: narrow sidebar with wave-line mark, MeteoSurf Cs, navigation "Jornada" selected, "Previsión", "Mapa", "Cámaras", then "Mis spots", and quiet bottom settings. Main title "Planificar jornada", subtitle "Castellón", action "Compartir previsión". Compact controls "Lun 23 nov", "09:00–12:00", "Surf", "Nivel: iniciación". Visible understated label "Propuesta · Datos de ejemplo".
Center the useful content: a precise generous comparison table with three actual place names "El Gurugú", "Heliópolis", "Morro de Gos". Columns "Ola estimada", "Periodo", "Viento", "Rachas"; example rows "0,4–0,7 m / 6 s / 5 kn NO / 8 kn", "0,3–0,6 m / 6 s / 6 kn NO / 9 kn", "0,5–0,8 m / 7 s / 7 kn N / 11 kn". Select El Gurugú with a pale blue row and check. Below, hourly forecast with labeled metre axis, hours 06 09 12 15 18, blue model curve, subtle selected 09–12 band, a separate wind row. No confidence percentages or quality stars.
Right-hand inspector shows "El Gurugú", a small believable Mediterranean beach camera preview labelled "Cámara simulada", clear play control, then "Observación de boya", "Hs 0,6 m", "Hace 18 min", "Previsión ECMWF", "Actualización 06:00". Include a quiet status "Heliópolis: observación no disponible" and note "El nivel no determina la seguridad". Prioritize actual readable information and coherent standard controls, not ornament.

Edit the provided MeteoSurf desktop UI mockup, preserving its layout, typography, values, navigation, light appearance, and synthetic-data labels. Correct only scientific labels and chart semantics: change the comparison-table column heading "Ola estimada" to two-line "Ola en playa" / "estimada"; change the chart title to "El Gurugú · Mar abierto"; change chart y-axis "Ola (m)" to "Hs (m)"; legend becomes "Hs prevista · ECMWF"; make the blue modeled curve dashed and remove the broad translucent fill underneath it, keeping only the vertical 09–12 selected time band. The buoy observation Hs is still a separate measured-data example in the right panel and must not be plotted as a forecast measurement. All data remain visibly labelled "Propuesta · Datos de ejemplo". Do not redesign or add content.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity mobile web app screen for "MeteoSurf Cs" for surf schools and coaches planning a session. Portrait viewport, edge-to-edge app UI, no device bezel, no browser frame, no collage. Premium contemporary Apple-like clarity, white background, pale neutral grouped surfaces, one system sans, modest type scale, refined conventional controls, blue functional selection. Match a desktop product with navigation Jornada, Previsión, Mapa, Cámaras; DO NOT squeeze its desktop table onto mobile.
Real Spanish content in reading order: compact brand "MeteoSurf Cs", title "Planificar jornada", visible "Propuesta · Datos de ejemplo". Controls arranged comfortably in two rows: "Lun 23 nov", "09:00–12:00", "Surf", "Nivel: iniciación". Then "Comparar spots" and three substantial horizontal list rows with clear individual field labels: "El Gurugú" selected, "Ola estimada 0,4–0,7 m", "Viento 5 kn NO"; "Heliópolis", "Ola estimada 0,3–0,6 m", "Viento 6 kn NO"; "Morro de Gos", "Ola estimada 0,5–0,8 m", "Viento 7 kn N". These are estimates of surf at the beach, not buoy measurements. A small footer link "Ver periodo y rachas". Compact selected-location section "El Gurugú" with segmented control "Previsión / Cámara", Cámara selected, showing a believable small Mediterranean beach preview explicitly labelled "Cámara simulada" with play control. Below a clearly visible button "Compartir previsión". Fixed bottom navigation with exactly four icons and readable labels "Jornada", "Previsión", "Mapa", "Cámaras", Jornada active; generous safe-area spacing, nothing overlaps. No pupils, payments, commercial hero, star ratings, confidence percentages, or safe-for-beginners verdict. Show an achievable scrolling mobile composition, not tiny text to fit desktop density.

Edit this MeteoSurf Cs mobile UI mockup into a genuinely narrow mobile viewport, aspect ratio 9:19.5, e.g. 768x1664 output representing a 390 CSS-pixel-wide phone. No device bezel. Preserve light Apple-like visual language and Spanish product content, but correct responsive layout, NOT just rescale. Keep text at believable 15–17 CSS px body size and tap targets at least 44 CSS px. Modest 24 CSS px title "Planificar jornada". Compact brand "MeteoSurf Cs" with a simple blue single-line wave, NOT a new illustrated logo. Date and time selectors two columns, sport and level next row. Keep "Propuesta · Datos de ejemplo" legible. THREE full-width spot selection rows, each arranged in TWO LINES: top line radio + spot name; second line two aligned labeled values "Ola estimada" and "Viento". Names and values: El Gurugú / 0,4–0,7 m / 5 kn NO; Heliópolis / 0,3–0,6 m / 6 kn NO; Morro de Gos / 0,5–0,8 m / 7 kn N. First selected. Never put name and both measures in a single cramped horizontal line. Below rows quiet "Estimación en playa; no medición de boya." and link "Ver periodo y rachas". Then small section "El Gurugú", switch "Previsión / Cámara", Cámara selected, compact 16:9 beach thumbnail labeled "Cámara simulada". Bottom button "Compartir previsión", then four-tab navigation Jornada / Previsión / Mapa / Cámaras with recognizable consistent thin-line icons. The content may scroll: do not shrink all elements to fit everything artificially. No extra repeated sections. Keep comfortable spacing and believable phone proportions.
